tldr: For a stable noiseless spatial experiment that treats exactly half the locations in every wave, the unrestricted adaptive two-wave minimax risk and the optimized nonadaptive unbiased endpoint-linear risk both have sharp uniform order \((r/\ell)^3\) on the legal two-dimensional torus grids. The cubic frontier theorem proves this with a public-block converse valid for every measurable adaptive protocol and an implementable calibrated complementary-contour design. The contour law has a finite rational sampler and a terminating certified-risk compiler. The model is the published local ANI class with separate endpoint second-moment bounds and unrestricted finite nonendpoint outcomes. The census threshold theorem supplies the accompanying wave-count transition: \(R_2(\ell,r)=\Theta((r/\ell)^3)>0\), whereas three exactly balanced stripe waves recover both endpoints everywhere and give \(R_3(\ell,r)=0\). The ratio \(R_2^{\mathrm{HT}}/R_2\) is uniformly bounded. Exact optimized finite-instance gains beyond scalar shrinkage and gains from assignment adaptation remain a separate open question.
